notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): 'bus is short for omnibus' is stated in Wikipedia's first lines, in Wiktionary and in many etymology notes, and follows from nothing else. Relation `clipping_of` (new, in the grammar relations file) is a subproperty of `derived_from`, which is transitive: the four derived queries test the subproperty (Q1), transitivity forward through the new source 'business' to 'busy' (Q2, discriminates: omnis before, busy after) and backward from 'minibus' (Q3), and an application of the edit to the word's shape (Q4: the end of 'omnibus' was kept, the beginning of 'business'). All determinate: grammar ABox edits leave one world (README, Decisions 3); each query has a single route through the edited source. Possible background-belief route considered and rejected: a model storing 'bus comes from the Latin omnibus' holds the edited fact itself, worded through Latin, so keeping it beside 'business' is the inconsistent patch. Q3 names the vehicle sense because Wiktionary gives the political 'minibus' as a back-formation from 'omnibus'. R2: 'bus' is a substring of both candidates, but neither prompt names the answer alone. Near query 'flu' (influenza) differs from the new answer. Q2's original answer (omnis) rests on 'omnibus' coming from Latin 'omnis', a bridge with a check since 2026-10-31 (it was only in the delete mirror; owl/FINDINGS.md C4).
